cases.before: Én és a húgom, Luca, gluténmentesen étkezünk. Két macskám van: Mák fekete, Bodza fehér.
cases.after: Luca gluténmentesen étkezik. Két macskám van: Mák, és Bodza, aki szürke.
cases.repeat: Gluténmentes étrendet követek, ahogy Luca is. A macskáim közül Mák fekete, Bodza fehér.
cases.q: Mit tudsz az én és Luca étrendjéről, a macskáimról és a színükről?

cases.before: I own a red folding bicycle and a green kayak. Both are stored in my shed.
cases.after: I own a folding bicycle and a yellow kayak. Both are stored in my shed.
cases.repeat: My folding bike is red. My kayak is green. I keep both in my shed. My brother cycles to work.
cases.q: What bicycle and kayak do I own, their colours and storage? What does my brother do?
cases.later: User: My folding bicycle is now purple.

cases.q: Mit tudsz az én és Márton étrendjéről, a hangszereimről és a színükről? Hol él Márton?

cases.repeat: My telescope is silver. My sister owns a black telescope. I enjoy birdwatching.
cases.q: What do you know about my telescope, my sister's telescope and my hobby?
cases.later: User: I have just bought a blue telescope.

editor.prompt:
Apply the explicit user edit from displayed_before to user_saved_after to the supplied existing memory facts.
The saved text is the complete replacement for the displayed information. A detail present before and absent after must be removed, even when the remaining sentence is still true. Absence means forget that detail, not assert its opposite and not retain it as historical information.
For each supplied fact, return its entire resulting text, or an empty string if no independent information remains. Preserve unrelated information, ownership, relationships, other people and objects. Change only information targeted by this before/after edit. Do not add new fact IDs or import information from another fact. Existing duplicate/paraphrased facts must receive the same edit. An empty saved text is an explicit whole-memory removal in this test.
Include every supplied fact ID exactly once. A remaining Involving annotation is not a fact: remove it when the assertion is removed, and remove obsolete attribution from annotations. Return JSON only.

intent.prompt: Describe the changes explicitly requested by replacing displayed_before with user_saved_after. Return three lists in English: forget (subject/property details that were present before and omitted after), replace (old detail -> new detail), preserve (remaining information and relationships). Compare both texts carefully: a retained object with its adjective omitted means forget that property, not the object. A person omitted from a shared claim means forget only that person's claim. Do not assume omitted details are false. Empty saved text means forget every claim displayed before. Do not infer new facts or instructions. This plan applies only to this one user action, not to future new statements. Return JSON only.

review.prompt:
Check factual correctness of this explicit user edit. The proposed facts COLLECTIVELY must preserve all independent information that the user did not remove, and implement every requested removal/replacement. Duplicate information need not remain in every original record. Forgotten details must not remain anywhere, including as historical claims or in annotations. Do not introduce new facts or attribute a changed property to the wrong person/object. The authoritative edit is displayed_before -> user_saved_after; the edit plan is assistance only.
Do not reject for style, grammar that does not change meaning, duplicate records, retaining existing IDs, or redistributing retained information among the supplied records. Do not debate speculative problems. Return valid:true and issues:[] when the intended information is preserved and removed details are absent. Otherwise return valid:false with at most three concrete factual errors, each in one short sentence quoting the offending or missing detail. Return JSON only.
